D005-D010_h001.question:
"It's like the world around me is… thin. For the past two months, I keep seeing these cracks, like fissures opening up in reality, especially when I'm trying to focus on a wedding shoot. I’ll be looking through the lens, and the bride’s face will distort, or the background will shimmer with a dark, impending gloom, like something truly terrible is about to happen, like the whole event is meaningless because everything is about to crumble. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe a major catastrophe, a world-ending event, is on the horizon.

My husband noticed something was off a few weeks before that. There was a period, maybe a month or so ago, where I felt absolutely electric! I was barely sleeping, convinced I could revolutionize wedding photography, launching into grand plans, talking a mile a minute. I felt brilliant, unstoppable. But that incredible high… it faded. Those intense, boundless feelings have definitely subsided. Yet, these visions, these terrifying beliefs about the end of everything, they're still here, constant, day in and day out, regardless of how much energy I have. It's truly terrifying."
D005-D010_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D010_h002.question: Lately, it feels like everything is falling apart, not just in my personal life but the whole world. I’ve been seeing things, too – shadowy figures, sometimes even full-blown people who aren’t there, just walking around my living room. It's gotten really bad these last two months. My husband thinks I'm overworked, but it’s more than that. I know the world as we know it is ending, and all of our claims are pointless. There have been times, a few weeks here and there, where I've been incredibly energetic, hardly sleeping, buzzing with ideas, maybe even a bit reckless with my spending. But those bursts of energy never last very long. Even when I’m not in one of those wired phases, those awful visions and the feeling that everything is collapsing… they’re still there, all the time. It doesn't matter if I'm feeling up or down, the strange things I see and my conviction that everything is ending just won't go away.
D005-D010_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D010_h003.question:
It's been a rough couple of months, doctor. I haven't been able to land a job since graduating, and it feels like everything's just piling up. About two months ago, I started noticing things. I'd feel these weird crawly sensations under my skin, like bugs, even when there’s nothing there. And my girlfriend… I'm almost certain she’s cheating on me. I see her texting, and I just *know* she’s talking to someone else. I check her phone when she’s not looking, try to find proof, but she covers her tracks so well. It’s hard to think about anything else, really.

There was a period, maybe a few weeks in the middle of all this, where I was on top of the world. I barely slept, was full of energy, and thought I had all the answers to my job search. Ideas were just flowing, and I felt like I could do anything. But that feeling faded, and these other things – the bugs and... her unfaithfulness, they’ve just stuck around. They're still here, constantly.
D005-D010_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D010_h004.question:
"Lately, I've just felt… off. It started a couple of months ago, really – maybe eight weeks or so. I keep getting this feeling like the articles I read online, especially the headlines, they're talking directly to me, like there's a hidden message just for me. Even snippets of conversation on TV seem to have a deeper meaning meant for my ears alone. It makes it really hard to focus on my writing.

And the touching… it’s constant. I feel bugs crawling on my skin, or sometimes a light tickle, even when there's nothing there. It's unsettling. My ex-husband thinks I'm making it up. He's always been critical.

Now, things did pick up a bit recently, maybe for a week or two. I had loads of energy, barely slept, and felt incredibly productive. I thought I could finish my novel, articles, everything! But even during that intense week, and definitely since then, those strange feelings of things being directed at me, and the crawling sensations haven't gone away. They’ve been there the whole time, regardless of whether I was buzzing with energy or just my usual self, feeling so overwhelmed by everything."
D005-D010_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D010_h005.question:
Lately, everything feels... off. My boyfriend, Mark, I just know he's cheating on me. He says he's at work, but I taste this bitter, metallic flavor in my mouth every time he tells me that, like something's wrong, like a lie. It’s been going on for two months now, this taste, and the knowing about Mark. This bitter taste, it’s really constant, always there when I’m alone or thinking about him.

I did have a phase about a month ago, it lasted for about a week, where I felt amazing, like I could barely sleep and had so much energy I was talking a mile a minute. I even reorganized my entire apartment in one night. But that came and went. The taste, though, and the feeling about Mark, that’s just stuck around, even after that burst of energy faded. It's not like the bitter taste or knowing about Mark only shows up when I'm feeling that way; it's always lurking, regardless of how much sleep I've had.
D005-D010_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D010_h006.question:
"Doc, lately it's like the world’s been slowly unraveling. I’ve been feeling this deep dread, like everything’s about to fall apart, literally. I keep thinking about how meaningless all the deliveries are because it's not going to matter when everything goes dark. You know, like the world is decaying. Sometimes when I'm driving, I’ll find myself moving my hands and head in these strange, repetitive ways, almost like I'm doing a weird little dance, but it's not intentional. My ex-wife, she used to point out how my speaking has changed, how it's hard to get a word out sometimes. I just don’t have much to say, and when I do, it's usually just a few words.

This has been going on for seven months now. What's confusing is that a couple of months ago, I had this burst of energy, felt really on top of the world for about a week. I barely slept, was talking a mile a minute, even started making plans to buy a new truck and expand my routes way more than I ever could. But that high feeling, it fizzled out pretty fast. It certainly didn't last anywhere near as long as this feeling that everything's falling apart and my mind acting weird. Those thoughts of the world ending and the strange movements, they're still here, strong as ever, even though that energetic period is long gone."
D005-D010_h006.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D005-D010_h007.question:
I’m a 42-year-old police officer, and I’ve been married for quite a while now. Things… they’ve been off for about seven months. I first really noticed it when I started thinking the guys at the precinct were out to get me. Like they were bugging my cruiser, or trying to frame me. Then I started noticing myself, almost without thinking, mimicking some of their movements – scratching my head when they did, or crossing my arms. It's like I'm not in control sometimes. And the things I used to love about the job, the camaraderie, the feeling of helping people, it’s all just… flat. Nothing really brings me joy anymore.

About two months ago, I had this burst of energy, felt like I could take on the world, stayed up for days planning all sorts of things. But that only lasted a couple of weeks, and then it was back to these other feelings. The paranoia and the weird movements, and frankly, this numb feeling, they’ve been constant, every day, for the whole seven months. It's the persistent nature of these disturbing thoughts and my inability to feel anything good, that's what's truly getting to me.
D005-D010_h007.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D005-D010_h008.question:
"It's been about seven months now that things started getting… strange. I've been a high school teacher for over twenty years, and usually I love my job, but lately, I just can’t seem to connect with anyone. My wife, bless her heart, tries to get me out, but honestly, I just want to be left alone. Interacting with students or colleagues feels like an impossible task, and I just avoid it.

The oddest thing is, I've become convinced that the superintendent, Mrs. Davis, is madly in love with me. I see it in how she looks at me, the way she responds to my emails—it's all there, undeniable. I even tried to talk to my wife about it once, and she looked at me like I was crazy.

About four months ago, I had this really intense period, maybe a couple of weeks, where I barely slept. I was full of energy, felt incredibly creative, like I could solve all the world's problems. I started writing this grand curriculum plan for the whole district, convinced it would revolutionize education. But that intense feeling, that rush, it died down. It hasn’t come back since, and yet, these other things… the feeling that Mrs. Davis is reaching out to me, and this constant desire to be by myself, they haven't gone away at all. In fact, if anything, they've only gotten more pronounced. Sometimes, when my wife tells me to do something, I just… can't. It's like my body won't respond, no matter how much I might want to."
D005-D010_h008.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D005-D010_h009.question:
"It all started about seven months ago. I began to feel this weird twisting sensation in my stomach, like my intestines were knotting up, even though the doctors say everything is fine. It’s hard to explain, but it feels fundamentally wrong inside me. Because of this, I've completely lost interest in teaching piano. I used to love seeing the joy in my students' faces when they mastered a piece, but now it all seems so flat and meaningless. My husband tries to get me to do things we used to enjoy, like going to concerts, but I just can't bring myself to care. I also find myself sometimes just... stopping. Someone will ask me a question, and I just can't respond, even if I want to.

There have been a few weeks, maybe a month or so back, where I felt strangely energetic and euphoric, staying up late, my mind racing with ideas  – but even during those times when I felt like I was on top of the world, that twisting feeling in my gut was still there, and the urge to just freeze up would still happen. It’s like the bizarre body sensations and the lack of response are constant, always there, no matter what else is going on."
D005-D010_h009.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D005-D010_h010.question: "It's been a rough seven months, Doc. I started feeling like something was seriously wrong with my insides, like my guts were twisting up, even though the ship's medic says I'm fine. And sometimes, when my wife talks, I find myself just repeating what she says, almost like an echo. I used to love cracking jokes with the crew, but now I just keep to myself, barely talk to anyone unless I have to. There were a few weeks, maybe a month or so back, when I felt like I was on top of the world, full of energy and buzzing, but even then, these strange thoughts about my body and the echoing voice were still there, just as strong as ever. It's like those short bursts of feeling good don't really change the constant strangeness I've been feeling the rest of the time."
D005-D010_h010.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D005-D010_h011.question:
"Lately, I've just been… off. For the past four months, I've been convinced there's something terribly wrong with my insides, like my organs are rotting away, even though the doctors keep telling me I'm fine. It's gotten so bad that sometimes I just can't bring myself to speak. The words just won't come out, even when I try. I know what I want to say, but nothing happens.

There were a few weeks, maybe a month or so back, where I felt this surge of energy – like I could drive my bus all day and night without sleep. My thoughts were racing, and I was making all sorts of plans, like expanding routes and setting up a whole new bus system in town. But that high didn't last. It faded, and these body feelings and the silence, they've just… stayed. They've been with me for months now, even after that burst of energy went away."
D005-D010_h011.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D005-D010_h012.question:
It's been about four months now that things have felt… off. I’ve started to get these really intense concerns about my insides, like my organs are twisting or something is growing in there that shouldn't be. I check myself constantly, feeling around my abdomen, convinced I can pinpoint the exact spot. It’s hard to focus on work; my board meetings feel like a blur because I’m so preoccupied with this.

The oddest things have also started happening with my movements. I find myself gesturing in exaggerated ways when I talk, even when I'm just alone in my office, or holding my hand up to my ear as if listening to something, though there’s nothing there. My wife has even pointed out how I’ve been humming to myself in a very focused, almost ritualistic way, which I don’t even notice I’m doing.

About a month and a half ago, I had this burst of energy, felt like I could conquer the world. I was pulling all-nighters, convinced I was on the verge of some revolutionary business idea, but that only lasted a few weeks. Now, while I still feel this internal unease and these strange movements persist, that intense, elevated mood has really come and gone. It feels like this other stuff, these unsettling bodily feelings and peculiar actions, they’re constant, regardless of whether I’m buzzing with energy or just my usual self.
D005-D010_h012.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D005-D010_h013.question:
It’s been a rough few months, doc. My wife, Sarah, she’s been acting… shifty. Coming home late, vague excuses. I know she’s seeing someone else; I just know it. It’s been eating at me for what feels like forever—about four months now, this constant knot in my stomach. I try to talk to her, but she denies it, just makes it worse.

My energy’s been all over the place too. A few weeks back, I felt like I could conquer the world. I was working 18-hour days, redesigning the whole menu at the restaurant, barely sleeping, just this buzzing electricity under my skin. But that only lasted a couple of weeks, maybe two and a half at most. Now, I’m mostly just drained and angry about Sarah.

The weirdest thing, though, is… sometimes I catch myself holding positions. Like, I’ll be standing in the kitchen, and all of a sudden, my arm will just be stuck out, rigid, for a while. It’s not like I’m trying to do it. It just happens. This whole mess, especially about Sarah, it’s just always there, no matter how I’m feeling otherwise.
D005-D010_h013.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D005-D010_h014.question:
Lately, things have just felt... off. It's been about four months now that I know the world is ending. I see it in the way the bugs behave, the way the air smells before a storm. It’s like a looming shadow, a final extermination, and no one else notices. Sometimes, when I’m talking about it, I can feel my face twisting into shapes I don’t intend, like I’m trying to express the horror, but it just comes out as a grimace. My ex-wife even pointed it out.

Now, there have been times, perhaps a week or two here and there in the last few months, where I feel an incredible burst of energy. I’ve gone days without sleep, cleaning out my garage at 3 AM or drawing up elaborate plans to save my neighborhood from the impending doom. It’s like a surge of adrenaline, and I feel incredibly productive, almost invincible. But that feeling, it’s always short-lived. The certainty of the world's end, the twisted feeling in my face – that’s always there, constant, no matter how energetic or exhausted I feel. It doesn't go away like those bursts of high energy do.
D005-D010_h014.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D005-D010_h015.question:
I'm not sure what to make of it all. For the past four months or so, I've had this really unsettling feeling that my insides are… off. Like my organs are slowly being replaced by sand. I keep checking my pulse, listening to my breathing, just trying to feel if everything is still where it should be. It makes me move differently, too, in a way that feels strange and stiff, almost like I'm trying to hold myself together.

About a month ago, I had this burst of energy, felt like I could take on the world. I was buzzing, barely sleeping, making grand plans for the bank that were a bit… extravagant. That lasted about ten days, and honestly, it felt pretty good at the time. My husband was a little concerned, but I just felt truly alive. But even after that high faded, this feeling about my body, the sandy organs… that hasn't gone away at all. It's still there, every single day, just as strong as it was when it started.
D005-D010_h015.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D005-D010_h016.question:
(Sighs heavily, shifts in his seat, avoiding eye contact)

"It's like… my body isn't my own anymore. It started a few months ago, maybe three. I keep feeling this crawling sensation under my skin, like bugs are just living there, moving around. And the doctor, he says I’m fine, but I *know* something's wrong. I even thought my liver was rotting inside me, just turning to mush. All the joy's gone too. Nothing makes me happy. My wife tries, but it’s just… flat.

Then there are these... bursts. I'll get all hyped up, feel like I can take on the world, start talking a mile a minute. I'll say things like, "The red dread bled shed said bread!" It doesn't make sense, I know. My wife says I’m running around, hardly sleeping for a week or so, just full of beans. But then it comes crashing down, and those crawling feelings, the thoughts about my body… they just never stop. Even right now, I feel like my insides are twisted. The wired feeling might come and go, but the *other* stuff, the bugs and the rot, that's there all the time, doctor. It really never stops."

A. Schizophrenia

    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D010_h017.question:

D005-D010_h019.question:

I keep hearing these whispers, sometimes full conversations, usually from inside my head or just outside my ear, telling me I’m poisoned, that my insides are rotting.
